name: Li-ion Battery Current-Collector Foils: Aluminium & Copper Foil Localisation
scope: Battery-grade aluminium (cathode) and copper (anode) current-collector foil in India: demand, import dependence, policy (battery-component scheme, anti-dumping duty, storage VGF) and the listed companies building capacity.

summary.one_line: India still imports an estimated 80-85% of its battery foil. This week brought indirect demand support: the Cabinet approved a Rs 14,500 cr storage VGF with 40% domestic content, and a government-backed study puts copper foil's cost gap at 27%. The aluminium-foil anti-dumping duty lapses in 20 days with no Finance Ministry notification found, and the battery-component scheme is still not approved.
key_points: IndexBox (May 2026) estimates imports cover 80-85% of India's battery-foil demand in 2026. China supplies 50-55% of import volume, Japan 20-25% and South Korea 10-15%. IndexBox projects 18-22% CAGR over 2026-2035, reaching 25,000-35,000 t and INR 2,500-4,000 cr by 2035 (S1).

New this edition: the Cabinet approved a Rs 14,500 cr viability-gap-funding scheme for 92 GWh of grid storage, including 30 GWh of battery storage, over FY27-FY31. Battery-storage projects must meet a 40% minimum domestic-content requirement (S31). This supports domestic cell demand, and so foil demand, indirectly.

New this edition: a study by NETRA, ARCI, CSIR-NCL, IIT Madras and Deloitte, released by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, finds Indian battery components cost 18-61% more than imports (S29). Copper foil's estimated gap is 27% (S30). The study proposes three incentive designs, including a 50% capital subsidy (S29).

The roughly Rs 12,000-13,000 cr battery-component scheme covers cathode, anode, separator, copper foil and electrolyte, but not aluminium foil (S9, S10). As of early Nov 2026 it was in inter-ministerial consultation (S30), and searches on 25 Nov found no approval.

DGTR has recommended continuing anti-dumping duty of USD 93.53-976.99/t on aluminium foil of 80 µm and below from China, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia for five years (S22). The current duty runs to 15 Dec 2026 (S15). Searches on 25 Nov 2026 found no Finance Ministry notification.

Hindalco's Q2 FY27 release says the Aditya battery-foil plant is 'scaling up to optimal production levels', with no foil volumes disclosed (S26). SRF's roughly Rs 600 cr, 12,000 MTPA Phase I is due by 30 Sep 2028 (S6).
No listed Indian company produces copper battery foil. Hindalco holds a Nippon Denkai licence for electrodeposited copper foil (S11), but no company-confirmed capacity was found.
The market is not pricing a foil theme. Over six months to 23 Nov 2026, Hindalco fell 17.05% and SRF fell 3.77%, while Shyam Metalics rose 38.33% (S18, S19, S20).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: If the Finance Ministry notifies DGTR's recommendation, Hindalco, SRF Altech and Shyam Metalics' subsidiary Shyam Sel and Power keep five more years of duty protection. All three were applicants in the sunset review (S22).

Hindalco is first mover: its plant is commissioned and fed by its own FRP complex (S3) and is now ramping up (S26). It also holds the only disclosed copper-foil technology route among listed names (S11), so it is best placed if the component scheme is approved (S10).
The storage VGF's 40% domestic-content rule for 30 GWh of battery storage (S31) adds a policy-driven source of demand for Indian cells, and so for foil, alongside ACC-PLI.
Sodium-ion cells use aluminium foil on both electrodes and need an estimated 700-1,000 t per GWh, against 350-500 t for Li-ion (S16). SRF has explicitly targeted sodium-ion (S28).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: The duty decision is still open, with 20 days left. If the Finance Ministry does not notify by 15 Dec 2026, the duty lapses (S15, S22). China supplies 50-55% of India's battery-foil imports (S1).

Announced aluminium-foil capacity runs ahead of near-term domestic demand. Hindalco's 25,000 t (S4) plus SRF's 12,000 t Phase I (S6) compares with IndexBox's 12,000-16,000 t for 2030 (S1). Hindalco's own forecast is higher, at 40,000 t by 2030 (S5).

Domestic producers face structural cost gaps of 18-61% against imports, 27% for copper foil (S29, S30). Without the component scheme, which excludes aluminium foil, new entrants carry that gap themselves (S9, S10).
Foil is immaterial to group revenue. IndexBox's entire 2035 Indian market of INR 2,500-4,000 cr (S1) equals about 3-4% of Hindalco's Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 91,708 cr (S26; our arithmetic).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: The Finance Ministry customs notification on aluminium-foil anti-dumping duty, due before 15 Dec 2026 (S15, S22).

Expenditure Finance Committee and Cabinet approval of the battery-component scheme, its incentive design (capital subsidy versus operating incentive), and whether aluminium foil is added (S9, S29, S30).
Battery-storage VGF tenders and how the 40% domestic-content rule is defined for cells and components (S31).
Shyam Metalics' November sales release (early Dec 2026) for foil volumes (S27), and Hindalco's Q3 FY27 disclosures on battery-foil utilisation, customers or copper foil (S26).

sections.title: What battery foil is and why India imports it

blocks.text: In a lithium-ion cell, aluminium foil is the cathode current collector and copper foil is the anode current collector (S2, S9). IndexBox gives typical aluminium battery foil as 12-15 µm thick, with thinning targets of 12-15 µm for aluminium and 6 µm and below for copper. Standard electrodeposited copper is 8-10 µm, and ultra-thin 6 µm copper carries a ±1 µm tolerance (S1). Swarajya puts electrodeposited copper foil at 4.5-8 µm (S9). Chinese industry sources say power-battery aluminium foil is mostly 20, 15, 13 or 12 µm, and moving toward 10 µm and below (S16). Hindalco has developed four battery-grade alloys, including AA1100 and AA1060 (S4).

Qualification is set by the customer. Hindalco says each sample needs a minimum of a few months of testing across several stages (S2). IndexBox says buyers expect certificates covering tensile strength, elongation, surface roughness and thickness uniformity. It adds that existing small-scale domestic foil generally fails battery-electrode specifications for thickness tolerance, roughness and ductility (S1).

blocks.text: The ~4-5% bill-of-materials figure comes from Hindalco, which is a producer (S2). A Chinese trade source puts aluminium foil alone at 1.5-2.0% of Li-ion cost (S16). Neither source explains its basis, so both are shown and treated as indicative only. The NETRA study, released by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, draws on data from more than 20 Indian companies but does not disclose company-level figures (S29). Coverage of it gives no aluminium-foil cost gap.

IndexBox (report updated 1 May 2026) estimates that imports meet 80-85% of India's battery-foil demand in 2026. China supplies 50-55% of import volume, Japan 20-25% and South Korea 10-15% (S1). Its forecast is 12,000-16,000 t by 2030 and 25,000-35,000 t (INR 2,500-4,000 cr) by 2035, with a bull case above 40,000 t and a bear case of 15,000-18,000 t (S1). Hindalco's own forecast is higher, at 40,000 t of battery-grade aluminium-foil demand by 2030 (S5).

Downstream demand depends on cell plants. Under ACC-PLI (outlay INR 18,100 cr), 40 GWh of the 50 GWh target had been awarded by Mar 2026: Ola Electric 20 GWh, Reliance New Energy 15 GWh and Rajesh Exports 5 GWh. Only Ola's 1 GWh had been commissioned (S17). India imported USD 4.93 bn of lithium-ion batteries in 2025-26, 93.79% of it from China (S9). New this week: the Cabinet approved a Rs 14,500 cr VGF scheme for 92 GWh of grid storage over FY27-FY31, split into 60 GWh pumped hydro, 30 GWh battery storage and 2 GWh other technologies. Combined investment is expected at INR 97,600 cr, and battery-storage projects carry a 40% minimum domestic-content requirement (S31).

subsections.title: Trade protection and the battery-component scheme

items: Anti-dumping duty: DGTR has recommended a five-year continuation of duties of USD 93.53-976.99 per tonne on aluminium foil of 80 microns and below from China, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia. The Finance Ministry takes the final decision. The duty was first imposed in Sep 2021 (S22).

The existing duty was extended to 15 Dec 2026 while the sunset review was completed (S15). Searches on 25 Nov 2026 again found no Finance Ministry notification acting on DGTR's recommendation, which leaves 20 days before the duty lapses.
The sunset-review applicants were Hindalco, LSKB Aluminium Foils, Raviraj Foils, Shree Venkateshwara Electrocast, Shyam Sel and Power, and SRF Altech (S22).

Battery-component scheme size: about Rs 12,000 cr according to Outlook Business, citing The Economic Times in Jun 2026 (S10), or about Rs 12,000-13,000 cr according to Swarajya (S9). Scope is cathode, anode, separator, copper foil and electrolyte, with aluminium foil not listed (S9, S10). Hindalco said in May 2025 that no PLI covered its aluminium-foil project (S2).

Scheme status: as of 2 Nov 2026 it was under inter-ministerial consultation (S30), after Swarajya earlier reported it heading to the finance ministry's Expenditure Finance Committee (S9). The NETRA study's three incentive designs are: (1) a 25% capital subsidy plus a sales-linked incentive covering about 30% of the cost gap; (2) an operating incentive alone covering about 60% of the gap, 11-37% by component, for 5-7 years; and (3) a 50% capital subsidy on the Semicon India model (S29). These are proposals, not approved rates (S30).

blocks.text: The duty deadline is close. If no customs notification is issued by 15 Dec 2026, the protection lapses (S15). DGTR's recommendation (S22) is not binding on the Finance Ministry. The storage VGF the Cabinet did approve this month supports demand for domestic cells, not foil production directly (S31).

subsections.title: Hindalco: commissioned and ramping, but small relative to the group

blocks.text: Hindalco says the battery-grade aluminium foil facility it commissioned on 27 Jan 2026 is India's first. It draws input directly from the 1.7 lakh tpa FRP complex (Rs 4,500 cr combined) and is designed to support up to 100 GWh of cells (S3). The product page cites 25,000 t of annual capacity, a 2,400 t customer-qualification line near Nagpur, an upgraded Mouda foil mill with a battery slitter and test labs, and supplies to customers in Europe, the USA, Asia and India (S4). The Q2 FY27 release (6 Nov 2026) says the battery-foil and FRP plants at Aditya are 'scaling up to optimal production levels'. It gives no foil volumes, named customers or copper-foil update (S26).

Materiality is low. Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 91,708 cr, EBITDA Rs 13,757 cr and PAT Rs 7,533 cr (S26). IndexBox's entire 2035 Indian battery-foil market of INR 2,500-4,000 cr (S1) is about 3-4% of that single quarter's revenue (our arithmetic). On copper foil, Nippon Denkai licensed its electrodeposited Li-ion copper-foil technology to Hindalco, with royalties tied to Hindalco's sales (S11). ICICI Direct says Hindalco is setting up a battery copper-foil plant (S10), but no company-confirmed capacity was found. The NETRA study's 27% copper-foil cost gap (S30) shows why such a plant would rely on the component scheme.

SRF's 21 Oct 2026 approval is a project under its wholly owned subsidiary SRF Altech at the existing Jetapur, MP site, funded through debt and internal accruals, to add value-added products for energy storage and EVs (S6). AlCircle reports the foil will serve Li-ion and sodium-ion batteries and names no customers (S28). In Q2 FY27, SRF's Performance Films & Foil segment revenue rose 51% to Rs 2,122 cr, against consolidated revenue of Rs 4,904 cr (S7).

Shyam Metalics announced battery-grade foil in Sep 2023, with 12-20 µm product validated by third-party labs, but gave no battery-specific capacity (S12). Its 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil plant began commercial production on 16 Jul 2026 to serve packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S13). Aluminium-foil sales volume rose 22.2% year on year in Oct 2026 (S27). None of these disclosures separate out battery foil.

No source found confirms commercial battery-foil sales by Shyam Metalics. It stays in the commissioned bucket only because its foil capacity is operating and it claims battery-grade capability (S12, S13).

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Share-price returns to 23 Nov 2026
blocks.source: Source: ICICIdirect quote pages (S18, S19, S20)

blocks.text: Share prices do not track the foil theme. Hindalco is down 17.05% over six months despite record Q2 results (S18, S26). SRF is down 11.81% over one year even after the foil approval (S19). Shyam Metalics is up 38.33% over six months (S20), a move that steel-volume growth explains better than foil (S27). Coverage is thin. ICICI Direct named Hindalco as a potential copper-foil beneficiary in a battery-component note (S10). This week's searches again found no dedicated broker thematic on 'battery foil stocks', no broker note specifically on SRF's foil plant, and no rating rationale mentioning battery foil for any smaller listed company.

blocks.text: IndexBox's 'top participants' list names companies such as Exide, Tata AutoComp and Mahindra as foil players. That conflicts with its own text, which says no large-scale domestic foil plant operates, so those names are not used here (S1).

items: Trade: the duty continues only if the Finance Ministry notifies DGTR's recommendation before it ends on 15 Dec 2026 (S15, S22). Chinese copper-foil overcapacity, about 2.1 mn t against about 1 mn t of demand, can depress prices (S9).
Cost gap: domestic battery components cost 18-61% more than imports, 27% for copper foil (S29, S30). Incentive design is still being debated (S30).
Demand timing: 1 GWh of 40 GWh awarded under ACC-PLI had been commissioned by Mar 2026 (S17). IndexBox does not expect domestic commercial output before 2028-29 (S1).
Overcapacity: Hindalco's 25,000 t (S4) plus SRF's 12,000 t (S6) exceeds IndexBox's 2030 demand of 12,000-16,000 t (S1), so producers would need to export.
Qualification: testing takes a minimum of a few months per sample (S2), and no named cell-maker approvals have been disclosed (S4, S26).
Materiality: foil is a small part of revenue for all three producers (S1, S7, S26).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries
companies.role: Commissioned India's first battery-grade aluminium foil facility at Aditya, Odisha, in Jan 2026: 25,000 tpa supporting ~100 GWh, plus a 2,400 t qualification line near Nagpur (S3, S4). Holds a Nippon Denkai licence for electrodeposited copper foil (S11).
companies.impact: First mover, and the plant was scaling up in Q2 FY27 (S26). It was an applicant for the anti-dumping duty that DGTR has recommended continuing (S22), and it is the only listed name with a copper-foil route into the pending scheme (S10), where the cost gap is 27% (S30). Foil is immaterial against quarterly revenue of Rs 91,708 cr (S26).

companies.name: Shyam Metalics and Energy
companies.role: Aluminium-foil producer. Announced third-party-validated 12-20 µm battery foil in 2023 (S12) and started an 18,000 tpa, 6-40 µm foil plant at Sambalpur in Jul 2026 aimed at packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S13).
companies.impact: Its subsidiary Shyam Sel and Power was an anti-dumping applicant (S22). Foil volumes rose 22.2% year on year in Oct 2026 (S27), but no battery-foil volumes have been disclosed. The stock is up 38.33% over six months (S20).

companies.name: SRF
companies.role: Board approved a ~Rs 600 cr battery aluminium-foil plant through SRF Altech at its existing Jetapur, MP site: 12,000 MTPA Phase I by Sep 2028 and Phase II by Sep 2030 (S6), for Li-ion and sodium-ion cells (S28).
companies.impact: Adjacent to its Performance Films & Foil segment, whose Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 2,122 cr (S7). SRF Altech was an anti-dumping applicant (S22). Battery revenue starts only from 2028. The stock is down 11.81% over one year (S19).

companies.name: Ola Electric Mobility
companies.role: ACC-PLI beneficiary with 20 GWh awarded, and the only commissioned capacity (1 GWh) as of Mar 2026 (S17). IndexBox says Ola Cell Technologies is exploring backward integration into foil (S1).
companies.impact: Its cell ramp-up is the largest single driver of domestic foil demand, and any in-house foil plan would compete with merchant suppliers (S1, S17).

companies.name: Reliance Industries
companies.role: Reliance New Energy holds 15 GWh under ACC-PLI (S17), and IndexBox names it as exploring backward integration into foil (S1).
companies.impact: A potential large foil buyer, or a captive producer if it integrates. The storage VGF's 40% domestic-content rule (S31) adds a use for domestic cells. No company-confirmed foil plan was found (S1, S17).

companies.name: Rajesh Exports
companies.impact: It only adds foil demand once its gigafactory is commissioned, which had not happened as of Mar 2026 (S17).

companies.name: HEG
companies.role: Setting up a graphite anode facility. ICICI Direct sees it as a potential beneficiary of the same battery-component scheme that covers copper foil (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent, not a foil maker: scheme approval would move anode and copper-foil names together (S10, S30).

companies.name: Graphite India
companies.role: Signed an MoU with Maharashtra for a synthetic-graphite anode project. ICICI Direct names it as a potential scheme beneficiary (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent, not a foil maker: exposed to the same scheme-approval timing (S9, S10, S30).

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W47 edition, researched on 25 Nov 2026 with web searches and direct page fetches. New this edition: (1) Cabinet approval of the Rs 14,500 cr storage VGF with 40% domestic content for battery storage (pv magazine, S31). (2) The NETRA/ARCI/CSIR-NCL/IIT Madras/Deloitte battery-component cost-gap study, with the 18-61% range from Energetica (S29) and the 27% copper-foil figure from Lapaas Voice (S30). The full report was not opened, and a CXOToday copy returned HTTP 403. (3) Share-price returns refreshed from ICICIdirect pages showing 23 Nov 2026 closes, which match numbers.json prices (Hindalco Rs 900, SRF Rs 2,515, Shyam Rs 1,276). Re-checked this week and still unresolved: no Finance Ministry notification on the aluminium-foil anti-dumping duty (now 20 days from lapse), no EFC or Cabinet approval of the battery-component scheme, no company-confirmed copper-foil capacity, no new Hindalco customer qualifications, and no small-cap battery-foil producer or rating-rationale mention. Shyam Metalics' November sales release is not yet out. Dropped to keep the source list tight: the Sep 2026 Shyam volume item (Univest), the Q1 FY27 Shyam foil-volume item (AlCircle) and the 2022 SRF capex item. The other DGTR applicants (LSKB, Raviraj, Shree Venkateshwara) were not confirmed as listed and are excluded, so the confirmed producers are one large cap and two mid caps, and the small-cap gap reflects how early the niche is. The extra companies are cell makers (foil demand) and battery-component scheme peers (adjacent), labelled 'other'. 'Our arithmetic' marks simple derived figures. No ratings or price targets.
